To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electronic structure of hydrogen bonds is determined by the geometry of the O··O bond and that the O-H bond is not a rigid unit.
“the electronic structure of oxygen atoms is a key parameter of the hydrogen bond and determines its stability, geometry and transformations”.
the internal structure of hydrogen bond is not a constant, and it can transform, and the transformation of hydrogen-bond structure is coupled to the transformation of molecular structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and dynamics of hydrogen-bonded systems.
the internal structure and properties of hydrogen bonds.
the internal structure of the hydrogen bonds and its transformations, which are responsible for the macroscopic properties of the crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a hydrogen bond is an electronic structure of a molecule or ion, which can change in a crystal in a number of ways, depending on the local environment.
hydrogen bonding in solids is a complex phenomenon, and the hydrogen bond is not just a chemical bond between two atoms.
the hydrogen bond is a complex, multi-component and dynamic structure, and the transformations of its internal structure can be described by a set of parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrogen bonds, being the strongest chemical bonds, are not only the strongest, but also the most versatile chemical bonds.
the internal structure of the hydrogen bonds is a very important factor, determining the macroscopic properties of crystals.
the electronic structure of oxygen atoms is a key parameter for understanding the internal transformations of hydrogen bonds and the structural properties of crystals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a set of parameters, describing the internal structure of hydrogen bond, can be used for a better understanding of the role of hydrogen bonds in the formation of crystal structures, and for the interpretation of their properties.

hydrogen-bonding patterns, molecular arrangements, and thermodynamic properties are interdependent, and that the electronic structure of oxygen atoms can be used for a quantitative description of hydrogen bonds.
the hydrogen bond is an electronic structure phenomenon, and its transformations should be considered in the context of the electronic structure of oxygen atoms.
